notFormalized.book: With generalized maps as vertical arrows the diagram (10.24) commutes (left to the reader); an equivariant sc-smooth germ $q : O(X, x) \to O(X', x')$ with $q(g * z) = \gamma(g) * q(z)$, and its strong bundle lift $Q$.
notFormalized.instead: **Formalized** (2026-11-12; V10.53, V10.54; `Chapter10/GapP2_GDiagram.lean`, `GapP2_GDiagramLift.lean`). With the vertical arrows the generalized maps $i(P) = [W \xleftarrow{1} W \xrightarrow{P} X]$, the square (10.24) commutes in $\mathcal{EP}(E^{-1})$ (`SDiagram.square_10_24`, `GenSBMap.square_10_24`). For the data $(x'', a, b)$ of $\gamma$, the germ $q = Q_b \circ \psi \circ Q_a^{-1}$ on a natural representation $U(x)$ is sc-smooth, has $q(x) = x'$ and is $\gamma$-equivariant (`Diagram.exists_germ_q`). Its lift $Q = H_b \circ \Psi \circ H_a^{-1}$ is a local strong bundle map with $P' \circ Q = q \circ P$, (10.25), and is $\gamma$-equivariant on the natural lifts (`SDiagram.exists_lift_Q`). Both are stated for each choice of data, since they depend on the representative, as the text says (Findings, Chapter 10, items 51, 52).

notFormalized.title: Theorem 10.5.7, generalized strong bundle isomorphisms determined by their orbit maps
notFormalized.label: §10.5, Theorem 10.5.7, p. 508 (2017: Theorem 10.10, p. 367)
notFormalized.book: If both strong bundles have the local regularity property and $[D], [D']$ are generalized strong bundle isomorphisms with $|[D]| = |[D']|$, then $[D] = [D']$.
notFormalized.instead: **Formalized since the first edition of this page** (V10.67), as a statement that does not hold as we read it: the strong bundle of Remark 10.5.5 has the local regularity property, and $[\mathrm{Inv}] \neq [1_W]$ with the same orbit map. A version for effective strong bundles is not formalized (Findings, Chapter 10, item 58).
